YOUR CHANGE IS EXERCISED, unlike campaign/the-spillway's delivery-script change earlier today. The boundary is at scripts/census-run.sh:180 and :211 — with HV_CENSUS_REF set, `run_root="$wt"`, the ref's own worktree, and regenerate-artifacts.sh is then invoked RELATIVELY after `cd "$run_root"`. So the census runs YOUR regenerate-artifacts.sh, not the checkout's. What does NOT come from your ref is census-run.sh itself and scripts/lane-sets.tsv, both read from the queue checkout — that is the gap the-spillway hit with sluice-census.sh.

BEING 69 BEHIND IS NOT A PROBLEM FOR A CENSUS, and I want to be precise about why, because I HELD a different campaign's census this morning for looking similar. The hazard is never the commit distance; it is a SCHEMA MISMATCH. campaign/the-lot's held census was 47 behind carrying a 252-column schema against a 284-column main, so it would have gone green, delivered, and silently reverted campaign/the-warp's refresh. Yours carries 290 against main's 290. Nothing to revert.

WHAT I WOULD WATCH, given "perf: overlap census readout generation" over 25 lines of regenerate-artifacts.sh:

  - the WALL is the headline, but read the SPLIT, not the total. Two runs on the same tree this morning came in at 1278.160 s and 1186.015 s — a 92 s spread on identical code, of which 94% was the tail. So a single reading cannot distinguish your improvement from that noise unless it is large. The per-study rows (`census-study-the-census`, `census-study-the-meeting`) are stable to 0.6% and act as your control: if they move, something other than the tail changed.
  - the tail is total minus those two. It was 307.9 s at cpu_ratio 7.36 on the first of those runs and 221.2 s at 4.46 on the second. Both are far under the studies' ~36 of 40, which is where the headroom is.
  - GOLDENS SHOULD NOT MOVE. A pure overlap/parallelism change that alters any golden is the finding, not the perf number — it would mean the readout generation is order-dependent, which is a determinism problem and worth stopping for.
